title: Remove Duplicate Trial Signups by Email
prompt: Your developer tools platform occasionally records duplicate trial signups when users submit the registration form multiple times. The `trial_signups` table contains a `signup_id` (primary key), `email`, `signup_timestamp`, and `initial_seats`. Multiple rows with the same `email` are considered duplicates. Delete all duplicate rows, keeping only the EARLIEST signup (lowest `signup_timestamp`) for each email. If two signups for the same email have identical timestamps, keep the one with the lower `signup_id`. After deletion, return all surviving rows ordered by `signup_id`. Write a DELETE statement followed by a SELECT statement that shows the final table contents.
schema_ddl: CREATE TABLE trial_signups (signup_id INT PRIMARY KEY, email VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL, signup_timestamp TIMESTAMP NOT NULL, initial_seats INT NOT NULL);
example_input_data: INSERT INTO trial_signups (signup_id, email, signup_timestamp, initial_seats) VALUES (1, 'alice@devco.com', '2024-01-15 09:00:00', 5), (2, 'bob@startup.io', '2024-01-15 10:30:00', 3), (3, 'alice@devco.com', '2024-01-15 09:05:00', 5), (4, 'carol@techfirm.com', '2024-01-16 08:00:00', 10), (5, 'alice@devco.com', '2024-01-15 09:00:00', 8), (6, 'bob@startup.io', '2024-01-16 14:00:00', 3), (7, 'dave@solo.dev', '2024-01-17 11:00:00', 1);
hints: Consider using a window function to assign a rank to each signup within the same email group, ordering by timestamp and then by signup_id.
Use ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY email ORDER BY signup_timestamp, signup_id) in a CTE to identify which rows to keep (rn = 1) versus delete (rn > 1).

Write a CTE that numbers each row within its email partition, then DELETE FROM trial_signups WHERE signup_id IN (SELECT signup_id FROM cte WHERE rn > 1), followed by SELECT * FROM trial_signups ORDER BY signup_id.
answer_key: WITH ranked AS (SELECT signup_id, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY email ORDER BY signup_timestamp, signup_id) AS rn FROM trial_signups) DELETE FROM trial_signups WHERE signup_id IN (SELECT signup_id FROM ranked WHERE rn > 1); SELECT * FROM trial_signups ORDER BY signup_id;

_meta.scenario: a developer tools company tracking trial-to-paid conversion and seat expansion
